title: Doug McIlroy and the Unix Philosophy (1978)
explainer: In 1978, Bell Labs' Doug McIlroy, inventor of the Unix pipe, wrote down the design principles that had already emerged among early Unix developers: make each program do one thing well, and build programs to work together by passing plain text streams between them. For someone designing new developer tooling, this is a concrete design argument, not just shell trivia: small, composable tools with a stable, simple interface tend to outlive large monolithic ones, which is exactly the tradeoff a tooling designer has to weigh when deciding how much a new tool should try to do.

title: Conway's Law (1967)
explainer: In his 1967 essay 'How Do Committees Invent?', Melvin Conway observed that any organization that designs a system will produce a design that mirrors its own communication structure. For a developer-tooling designer, this is a direct warning: a tool built by one team in isolation tends to encode that team's own boundaries and assumptions, quietly forcing every other team that uses it to work around a structure they had no say in, so tooling decisions are organizational decisions whether or not anyone admits it.
